_comment: Packs for the el / la trainer (/articles), see src/lib/artikelPacks.js. `topics` groups the lexicon's own unit topics (src/content/lexicon/*.json; the topic ids stayed German) into everyday packs; a noun belongs to the pack of its FIRST topic, so every tagged noun is in exactly one. `rules` are gender patterns, checked in this order on the noun's first word; a noun joins a rule pack only if it matches the pattern AND its real article is the pack's article. The ones that match and break it are the exceptions (el día, la mano). `names` is a word list, `suffixes` are endings, `genusF` takes the feminine nouns with a stressed a- (el agua, lexicon genus: f). `min` lowers minPack for a rule with few nouns. `noRule` lists set phrases no ending rule speaks about; acronyms (IVA, ESO) are skipped by the code.
_levels: A topic pack's `levels` renames it per level: one lexicon topic holds different nouns at each level (A1 wohnen = kitchen, bathroom; A2 = deposit, landlord), so no pack name repeats across A1–B2. `name`/`icon` are the fallback.

rules.name: el + stressed a-
rules.rule: Feminine nouns that start with a stressed a- or ha- take el in the singular, so the two a sounds don't run together: el agua, el aula, el hambre. They stay feminine: el agua fría, las aguas.
rules.ruleLeicht: Some words start with a strong “a”. They take “el”, but they are feminine: el agua fría, las aguas.

rules.name: -ma words from Greek
rules.rule: Many words in -ma come from Greek and are masculine: el problema, el tema, el idioma, el sistema. Not every word in -ma: la cama, la forma, la crema.
rules.ruleLeicht: These words end in -ma, but they take “el”: el problema, el idioma.

rules.name: -ción and -sión
rules.rule: Nouns in -ción and -sión are feminine: la estación, la información, la televisión, la decisión.
rules.ruleLeicht: The word ends in -ción or -sión? Then you say “la”: la estación.

rules.name: -dad, -tad and -tud
rules.rule: Nouns in -dad, -tad and -tud are feminine: la ciudad, la universidad, la libertad, la salud.
rules.ruleLeicht: The word ends in -dad, -tad or -tud? Then you say “la”: la ciudad.

rules.name: -umbre
rules.rule: Nouns in -umbre are feminine: la costumbre, la cumbre, la legumbre.
rules.ruleLeicht: The word ends in -umbre? Then you say “la”: la costumbre.

rules.name: -aje
rules.rule: Nouns in -aje are masculine: el viaje, el garaje, el paisaje, el mensaje.
rules.ruleLeicht: The word ends in -aje? Then you say “el”: el viaje.

rules.name: -or
rules.rule: Most nouns in -or are masculine: el ordenador, el color, el conductor. The ones to watch: la flor, la labor.
rules.ruleLeicht: The word ends in -or? Then you usually say “el”: el color.

rules.name: -o
rules.rule: Most nouns in -o are masculine: el libro, el trabajo, el vaso. The ones to watch: la mano, la foto, la moto, la radio.
rules.ruleLeicht: The word ends in -o? Then you usually say “el”: el libro.

rules.name: -a
rules.rule: Most nouns in -a are feminine: la casa, la silla, la mesa. The ones to watch: el día, el mapa, el planeta, el tranvía.
rules.ruleLeicht: The word ends in -a? Then you usually say “la”: la casa.
